books.title: Architecture
books.description: Dependency direction and who may write state.

books.title: Testing
books.description: How tests are linked to specs and rules.

books.description: Code conventions that need judgement, checked by an agent.

books.description: Agent reviews of the rules and tests themselves.

rules.title: No assembly cycles
rules.rule: The asmdef reference graph under Assets/Framework has no cycles.
rules.why: A cycle makes two features one feature and blocks every layering rule.
rules.fix: Move the shared type down to a lower assembly, or invert the dependency with an event or an interface.

rules.title: Layer references
rules.rule: Each Framework runtime assembly references only the Framework assemblies listed for it.
rules.why: Keeps Core and Wire free of domain features, and makes every new dependency a visible decision.
rules.fix: Remove the reference, or add it to this rule's table if the new direction is intended.

rules.title: No framework dependency on spikes
rules.rule: No Framework assembly references a spike or prototype assembly.
rules.why: Spikes are deleted in roadmap phase 8. The framework must not need them.
rules.fix: Promote the needed type into Assets/Framework, following docs/feature-layout.md.

rules.title: InternalsVisibleTo allowlist
rules.rule: Each Framework runtime assembly grants internal access only to the assemblies listed for it.
rules.why: Store writers are internal. Every grant widens who can write state.
rules.fix: Remove the grant. If a new assembly needs internal access, add it to this rule's table and say why in the PR.

rules.title: Only apply handlers write stores
rules.rule: An internal method on a Framework store is called only from a WireEventHandler<T> subclass.
rules.why: Server and client build the same state only when the same apply handler writes it.
rules.fix: Emit a wire event from the service. Let the apply handler for that event call the store writer.

rules.title: Apply handlers do not call services
rules.rule: A WireEventHandler<T> subclass does not call a Framework service.
rules.why: Apply handlers run on the client too, where services do not exist. A handler only writes its store.
rules.fix: Move the service call out of the handler, for example into a server-only listener on the event stream.

rules.title: GameEngine exposes read-only views
rules.rule: GameEngine exposes only services, read-only store views, the event stream and the network.
rules.why: Callers author through services and read through views. A writable store on the engine bypasses the apply handlers.
rules.fix: Expose the store through its IReadOnly* interface instead of the concrete store type.

rules.title: Every feature has tests
rules.rule: Each feature folder with a Runtime folder has a Tests or PlayTests assembly with at least one test.
rules.why: A feature without its own tests is only covered by accident.
rules.fix: Add Framework.<Feature>.Tests with at least one unit test. Follow docs/testing.md.

exceptions.reason: Tag tests live in Framework.Entities.Tests; Framework.Tags.Tests is empty.
GameEngine is a plain aggregate, covered by Bootstrap and integration tests.

rules.title: Wire holds no domain events
rules.rule: Framework.Wire declares no WireEvent subtypes except the Block events.
rules.why: Wire is a transport. Domain events live with the feature that owns them.
rules.fix: Move the event into the feature assembly that emits it.

rules.title: Acceptance tests and pictures are paired
rules.rule: Every acceptance test has a [Picture] that names an existing scenario file, and every scenario file has a test. Files that start with "_" are guides, not scenarios.
rules.why: The picture is the spec. A test without a picture, or a picture without a test, drifts from the intent.
rules.fix: Add [Picture("<scenario>.md")] to the test, or write the binding for the scenario. Follow docs/testing.md.

rules.title: Client converges with server
rules.rule: A command run on the server leaves the client with the same events and the same store values.
rules.why: The client builds state only from the server's events. Convergence is the core promise of the wire.
rules.fix: Check that the event reaches the client channel and that the same apply handler is registered on both sides.

rules.title: Comments warn, they do not narrate
rules.rule: A code comment in the runtime code of Assets/Framework (each feature's Runtime folder) warns about something the code does not show. It does not restate the signature or the body.
rules.why: docs/coding-standards.md: narration goes stale and hides the comments that matter.
rules.fix: Delete the comment, or rewrite it as one line that warns about the non-obvious fact.

params.subject: files
params.prompt: Read docs/coding-standards.md section "Comments". Then review the C# files listed under Subject. Report each comment that narrates (restates what the code or its name already says, or is a header block that describes the type). Do not report comments that warn about an invariant, an ordering constraint, a workaround or a non-obvious reason.

rules.title: Rules are well written
rules.rule: Each rule in the rulebook states one checkable thing, gives a real reason, gives a fix an engineer can act on, and its check matches its statement.
rules.why: A vague rule or a check that tests something else gives false confidence.
rules.fix: Rewrite the rule statement, why or fix, or change the check parameters so they test exactly what the statement says.

params.subject: rules
params.prompt: Review every rule under Subject. For each rule decide: (1) the statement says one checkable thing, (2) why gives a real consequence, (3) fix is an action an engineer can take, (4) the check kind and params test exactly what the statement says, not more and not less. Use Tools/Rulebook/README.md for what each check kind does. Report only rules with a real problem; target is the rule id.

rules.title: Linked tests prove their rule
rules.rule: Each test that carries [Rule("ID")] would fail if the rule it names were broken.
rules.why: A linked test that passes whatever the code does makes the rule look enforced when it is not.
rules.fix: Add the missing assertion to the test, or remove the [Rule] link and attach a test that does prove the rule.

params.subject: linkedTests
params.prompt: For each rule under Subject, find its linked tests in the source (Grep for the test class and method names). Decide whether each test would fail if the rule were broken. Report tests that would still pass, and say which assertion is missing. Target is the test full name.

rules.title: Acceptance bindings match their pictures
rules.rule: Each acceptance binding performs the Given and When of its picture, asserts every Then and Invariant line, and performs no step the picture does not describe.
rules.why: The picture is the spec. A binding that skips a Then line leaves that behavior untested.
rules.fix: Add the missing step or assertion to the binding, or correct the picture if the intent changed.

params.subject: pictures
params.prompt: For each picture and binding pair under Subject, compare the picture lines (Given, When, Then, Invariants) with the binding code. Report each Then or Invariant line that the binding does not assert, and each binding step that the picture does not describe. Target is the picture file name.
